description: Mustafa Senkaya and collaborators publish a 44-location table of building damage status after the February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye. Its six ground and shaking predictors include Vs30, engineering bedrock depth, predominant frequency, peak ground acceleration and two distance measures. The author-named Zenodo version-one page lists a 13.8 kB XLSX workbook with free public access and CC BY 4.0. Building-risk simulations can use the rows as a small benchmark for checking damage classifiers or comparing ground-condition and shaking predictors. The sample is limited to available AFAD station locations in three affected provinces, so the paper's high model scores do not establish wider predictive accuracy. The journal says data are on author request, but the later public deposit provides a separate route; the workbook itself was not downloaded or inspected. The catalogue Türkiye 2023 building-damage resource is related but covers a different, larger compilation of footprints, assessments and environmental factors.
name: Modeling the Importance of Ground and Strong-Motion Variables on the Damage Status in the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes Using Supervised Machine Learning
notes: G4-0637; G4 other data journals. Metadata only. Simulation uses are reviewer assessments. Data payloads and code execution were not checked.
